主要内容: In June 2014, the average cost per hour worked for employee compensation among private industry employers varied significantly by major occupational group. For instance, in management, professional, and related occupations, employers spent an average of $53.52 per hour worked, with $37.20 for wages and salaries and $16.33 for benefits. In contrast, service occupations had employer costs of $14.10 per hour, with $10.72 for wages and salaries and $3.39 for benefits. Overall, employers spent an average of $30.11 per hour worked for employee compensation, with wages and salaries accounting for 69.8 percent of these costs and benefits making up the remaining 30.2 percent. These data are from the Employment Cost Trends program and are detailed in the report 'Employer Costs for Employee Compensation — June 2014'.
